# Exercise 1a: Composite functions in R

```{r}
fx <- function(x) 2*x^2 - 4
gx <- function(x) 7*abs(x) + 3

xx <- seq(-5, 5, length.out = 200)

data.frame(
  x        = xx,
  `f(x)`   = fx(xx),
  `g(x)`   = gx(xx),
  `f(g(x))` = fx(gx(xx)),
  `g(f(x))` = gx(fx(xx)),
  check.names = FALSE
) |>
  pivot_longer(-x, names_to = "fun", values_to = "y") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y, color = fun)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.3, color = "black") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.3, color = "black") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-10, 50)) +
  labs(x = "x", y = "y = f(x)", color = NULL)
```

# Exercise 1b: Composite functions in R

```{r}
fx <- function(x) sin(x)
gx <- function(x) log(x)       # natural log (same as np.log)
hx <- function(x) 2*x^2 + 5

xx <- seq(-100*pi, 100*pi, length.out = 1001)
f3 <- fx(gx(hx(xx)))

ggplot(data.frame(x = xx, y = f3), aes(x, y)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "x", y = "y = f(x)", title = "f(g(h(x)))")
```

# Exercise 2: Inverse function in R

```{r}
# f(x) = log(2x), g(x) = exp(x)/2  — f and g are inverses of each other
fx <- function(x) log(2*x)
gx <- function(x) exp(x)/2

xx <- seq(0.01, 5, length.out = 50)

data.frame(
  x         = xx,
  `f(x)`    = fx(xx),
  `g(x)`    = gx(xx),
  `f(g(x))` = fx(gx(xx)),
  `g(f(x))` = gx(fx(xx)),
  check.names = FALSE
) |>
  pivot_longer(-x, names_to = "fun", values_to = "y") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y, color = fun)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-5, 10)) +
  labs(x = "x", y = "y = f(x)", color = NULL)
```

# Exercise 3: Composite functions — building and plotting numerically

In Python, SymPy builds and renders a symbolic expression. In R, we define
functions and evaluate them directly — the composition is the same idea.

```{r}
# Build f(g(h(x))) = sin(log(2x^2 + 5)) as nested R functions
fx <- function(x) sin(x)
gx <- function(x) log(x)
hx <- function(x) 2*x^2 + 5

xx <- seq(-100, 100, length.out = 500)

ggplot(data.frame(x = xx, y = fx(gx(hx(xx)))), aes(x, y)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "x", y = "f(g(h(x)))",
       title = expression(y == sin(log(2*x^2 + 5))))
```

# Exercise 4: Inverting functions in R

```{r}
# f(x) = 2x + 3 → inverse is f_inv(y) = (y - 3) / 2
fun    <- function(x) 2*x + 3
invfun <- function(y) (y - 3) / 2

# Composing f with its inverse should recover the original value
cat("f(f_inv(4)) =", fun(invfun(4)), "\n")
cat("f_inv(f(4)) =", invfun(fun(4)), "\n")
```

```{r}
# For functions without a closed-form inverse, use uniroot()
# Example: find x such that fun(x) = 4 numerically
target <- 4
result <- uniroot(function(x) fun(x) - target, interval = c(-10, 10))
cat("Numerical inverse: x such that f(x) = 4 is", round(result$root, 6), "\n")
```
